articles.title: Five-set tennis is under attack. Killing it would be a colossal unforced error | Andrew Lawrence
articles.summary: Five-set matches are physically punishing, occasionally absurd and increasingly under threat. They also produce much of what makes grand slam tennis great. Tuesday night’s quarter-final match between Ben Shelton and Carlos Alcaraz had everything a US Open spectacle could ask for: huge stakes…
body: Somewhat predictably, the discourse among media and fans following the late-night match has swiftly moved on from the USTA’s misadventures in scheduling to a referendum on the five-set match and whether it should be put out to pasture. For the record: that would be a colossal unforced error.

Five-setters aren’t just intrinsic to the grand slam canon. They are a badge of honor in the men’s game, confirmation that a player can and did indeed hack it in the big leagues. John Isner may not have won a major during his time on tour. But his capacity for grinding out marathon matches – not least the three-day, 11-hour epic he played against Nicholas Mahut at Wimbledon in 2010 – is why he remains highly respected by peers and fans alike.

Best-of-five is the exclusive framing device for the best matches in history and an imprimatur of the sport’s most revered champions. (See, The Greatest Match Ever Played or last year’s French Open final.) Even the losers are celebrated merely for having survived and played on to become part of the tale. “People still remember this match but he didn’t know if I was the winner,” Mahut said in 2015. “So, maybe, in 10 years people will think I won the match.”
points: Five-set matches are physically punishing, occasionally absurd and increasingly under threat.
They also produce much of what makes grand slam tennis great.
For the record: that would be a colossal unforced error.
“People still remember this match but he didn’t know if I was the winner,” Mahut said in 2015.

articles.title: Chess: Uzbekistan favourites for Olympiad but ageing England given gloomy outlook
articles.summary: England Open squad have internal tensions but the women’s team blends rising talent with experience. Uzbekistan, the host nation, are the favourites to win the 208-team biennial chess Olympiad in Samarkand, which has its opening ceremony on Tuesday, and its first round (of 11) on Wednesday.
body: The defending champions, India, China and the US are Uzbekistan’s most dangerous rivals. India would have been the open Olympiad favourites but for the shaky form of the world champion, 20-year-old Gukesh Dommaraju, who was the top board gold medallist in Budapest two years ago but is likely to play lower down the order in Samarkand. USA are led by the world No 3 Fabiano Caruana and the world No 5 Wesley So, but their lower boards, including the variable Hans Niemann, look more vulnerable.

England, with an ageing squad, may struggle to reach the top 15, although they are seeded 12th. The oldest England player, nine-time British champion Michael Adams, is 54. Luke McShane is 42, Nikita Vitiugov and Gawain Jones are in their late 30s, while Daniel Fernandez, making his England debut, is 31. It is likely that the selectors would have chosen 17-year-old Shreyas Royal had they known that he would win the British championship, but that event was in August while Fide’s nomination deadline was in mid-July.

articles.title: Why Nigel Benn can't walk away from Conor
articles.summary: Nigel Benn vowed to leave son Conor to plough his own path after he beat Chris Eubank Jr, but the retired world champion is back by his side this week as he prepares to face WBC welterweight champion Ryan Garcia.
body: Nigel Benn had insisted he was stepping away from his son's career for good.
The 10,000-mile trips from Australia - where Nigel is based - were done, and Conor Benn was on his own after his grudge-match win over Chris Eubank Jr.

Yet in the build-up to Conor's WBC welterweight world title challenge against Ryan Garcia in Las Vegas, the 'Dark Destroyer' was by his son's side at the news conference and holding court at their Essex media day - as embedded as ever.
Ask Nigel why and he claims Conor "twisted my arm" into helping with one final hurdle.

articles.title: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan cool on NFL return to Australia: ‘I just don’t like to travel’
articles.summary: San Francisco boss hesitant for team to play another game in Melbourne. LA Rams head coach Sean McVay refuses to blame travel plan for loss. Victorious San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan said he loves Australia, the “gladiator-ish” MCG and its surface, the local hospitality and the…
body: After the 49ers’ 27-7 victory over the LA Rams in the first NFL match in Australia, the 46-year-old revealed he wants to come back to holiday and see more of the country than this week’s goldfish bowl routine of hotel-to-practice-to-hotel would allow.
But in the media conference after winning, the follow-up question was more pointed. Would he want to come back, not to visit, but to play?

Another pause, the awkwardness growing by the second. Then, a joke to relieve the tension. “I’d like 17 home games in San Francisco,” he said with a wide smile. Finally, 10 seconds after the question was asked, he got to the point.
It’s the debate the NFL’s international expansion hinges on, amplified by the remoteness of Australia.

articles.title: Ashes legal dispute: Hampshire damages claim led to lack of 2027 Test in north of England
articles.summary: Hampshire paid £1m by ECB after missing out in 2023. County challenged decision to give Headingley match. The lack of Ashes cricket in the north of England next summer is the result of a legal dispute that followed the allocation of venues for the 2023 series against Australia, which also involved…
body: The Guardian can reveal that Hampshire brought a legal challenge against the ECB after missing out on hosting the Ashes in 2023 to Yorkshire, who staged the third Test – which England won by three wickets – at Headingley.

Hampshire are understood to have challenged the 2023 allocation on the grounds the club said they were promised their first Ashes Test at the Rose Bowl that year at a meeting of the 18 first-class counties in 2018, alongside matches at Old Trafford, Edgbaston, Lord’s and the Oval, with Headingley to be given a Test in 2027 instead.

The Guardian has been told the ECB’s original plan had been to award Old Trafford and Headingley one Ashes Test apiece in 2023 and 2027 respectively, but that decision was changed after a report from a four-person independent panel. It recommended the Test that had been pencilled in for Hampshire should take place at Headingley.

articles.title: Is triple Chelsea attack worth it? FPL gameweek four dilemmas
articles.summary: BBC Sport FPL expert Holly Shand looks at some of the biggest dilemmas facing FPL managers heading into gameweek four, including whether to captain Erling Haaland or a Chelsea player.
body: The Fantasy Premier League season is entering week four and plenty of managers will be getting itching fingers, with so many chips at our disposal.

Chelsea striker Joao Pedro (£7.7m) is the most-owned player in the game, in 72.5% of sides. Given that Chelsea have scored eight goals already this season, and face promoted Hull City at home next, it feels like the right time to be moving towards a double up on their assets.

Cole Palmer (£9.6m) and Morgan Rogers (£7.6m) came on as half-time substitutes in the Carabao Cup against Leeds United on Wednesday, with Palmer scoring a double including a penalty, and Rogers chalking up three assists.
Palmer has the edge, if you can afford him, given his greater goal threat and penalties.

body: While an away defeat to Como isn't necessarily cause for alarm on its own, the manner and margin of the loss should concern Demichelis and his superiors. Leipzig repeatedly left themselves exposed by playing a high defensive line, with Como able to exploit the space in behind on several occasions.

“We really took a beating tonight. The first half wasn’t good at all, while the second half was a tad better. Overall, however, it was a poor performance from us. We need to learn from this and make some changes as soon as possible," he said.

The expectation will be for Leipzig to respond immediately with a home victory against bottom-placed Hamburger SV on Sunday. They can take confidence from their recent record against Die Rothosen, having won each of their last four meetings.
It has been a disastrous start to the season for Hamburger SV, who sit rock bottom of the Bundesliga table with 0 points and a 0-7 goal difference following their first two matches.

body: It was the NFL's first game in the Asia-Pacific region, and its longest-ever road trip for the first of a record nine international games in 2026.

Sean McVay's side are Super Bowl favourites after acquiring defensive end Myles Garrett and welcoming one of the NFL's greatest defensive players, Aaron Donald, out of retirement.

"I love when they [the Rams] came out and they were booing. We were out here for a week. We enjoyed the city. I don't think you can fly 16 hours and be ready to play," 49ers receiver Deebo Samuel told Australia's Channel Seven.

articles.title: Back to Europe? Juan Mata leaves Australia and weighs up future
articles.summary: The Asturian midfielder Juan Mata has officially confirmed that he will no longer wear the Melbourne Victory shirt. After a single but spectacular season in Australia’s A-League, the veteran footballer has decided to bring his spell on the other side of the world to an end and carefully consider…
body: At 38 years old, the World Cup winner with Spain wraps up a brilliant stint in the Oceanian league. Mata was awarded the Johnny Warren Medal, the honor that recognizes him as the best player in the Australian championship. During his time in Melbourne, he posted outstanding numbers, recording 5 goals and 13 assists in 24 matches played.

Despite his departure from the pitch in Australia, the Asturian will maintain a close institutional link with the club. Mata is part of Melbourne Victory's shareholder group and will take over as president of the club 's new football committee, an executive role he will combine with deciding whether to extend his playing career in Europe.

The player himself expressed his gratitude to the club and the fans in his public farewell. "I enjoyed every minute and fell in love with football again in a very special place," said the former player of clubs such as Chelsea, Manchester United, and Valencia CF.

articles.title: U.S. Open Gave Creators A Pass. FIFA & TikTok Gave Them A Role. Wimbledon Passed
articles.summary: Amid the latest U.S. Open creator controversy, Wimbledon does not plan dedicated creator accreditation for 2027, unlike U.S. Open and FIFA-TikTok models.
body: Wimbledon has answered the U.S. Open’s creator controversy by declining to create the category. The All England Club does not plan to introduce a dedicated accreditation for influencers or content creators at the 2027 tournament, and will confiscate equipment such as ring lights under its existing conditions of entry, according to a Press Association report.
Its ticket terms for 2027, updated on September 1, already bar ticket holders from any “live or as live dissemination” of match audio or video.

It is a tidy response to an untidy fortnight in New York, but the three organizations are answering different questions. The U.S. Open created a credential that gave creators access. The FIFA-TikTok program went further: it defined what creators could cover, where they could go and what they could not film. Wimbledon is choosing not to create a separate creator category at all.

The disruption that started the argument, during Naomi Osaka’s first-round match, did not come from credentialed creators. The people the chair umpire asked to sit down were not part of the creator program, Brendan McIntyre, the USTA’s head of communications, said in a statement to ABC News.

articles.summary: FC Barcelona head coach Hansi Flick has surpassed club legend Johan Cruyff with an impressive record. As the back-to-back La Liga champions, the Blaugrana have started 2026/2027 in roaring fashion with four wins out of four.
body: Three of those victories have seen Barca raise a “manita” by scoring five goals, and they also did that in the Champions League in torrential rain on Wednesday by putting the same amount of strikes past Feyenoord while the Dutch could only respond with one.
Speaking of the Eredivisie giants, they were Cruyff’s last club as a player in the mid-1980s before he went into coaching.

He first manned the Ajax dugout, and then returned to start a revolution at FC Barcelona in 1988 which took in a revamp of La Masia and the club’s playing style, its maiden Champions League crown at Wembley, and four consecutive La Liga triumphs.
With two Spanish top fights under his belt, Flick is on the road to emulating the “Eternal Johan”, who passed in 2o16.

articles.title: Rybakina denies Gauff to set up blockbuster US Open final with Sabalenka
articles.summary: American hearts were broken as Elena Rybakina silenced Coco Gauff and the New York crowd to set up a blockbuster US Open final against Aryna Sabalenka, who defeated Jessica Pegula to move a win away from her third straight title at Flushing Meadows.
body: Rybakina battled back to upset home favourite Gauff 3-6 6-4 6-4 in a fierce semi-final showdown to secure a ​title showdown with defending champion Sabalenka and stay ​on course for a ‌third Grand Slam crown.
Sabalenka had beaten Gauff's American compatriot Jessica Pegula 7-5 6-2 ‌earlier in the night to close in on a ​rare three-peat in New York.

"Of course there were nerves," admitted Rybakina in her on-court interview. "Coco is a great player. It's always tough to play her. Even if sometimes her first serve doesn't go the second one is so heavy it's difficult to dictate the rallies. I took a deep breath, tried to talk positive with myself and just told myself I need to fight and try to show good tennis."

Gauff absorbed relentless pressure ​but stayed strong to draw errors from the Kazakh, ​breaking in the sixth ⁠game and taking the ⁠opening set in front of a passionate crowd ‌that included former first lady Michelle Obama.

articles.title: 'A great sporting ticket' - US Open chief vows to keep day, night session format
articles.summary: US Open chief Craig Tiley has told Sky Sports Tennis he plans on keeping two matches during the day and two at night at Flushing Meadows in 2027.
body: Tiley, who took the helm as new CEO of USTA earlier this year after leading Tennis Australia since 2013, says he has no plans for any changes to the schedule.

It comes after Ben Shelton's five-set thriller against Carlos Alcaraz in the quarter-finals ended at 3:33am local time on Wednesday, leaving few people awake to see the near five-hour marathon reach its finale on one of the sport's biggest stages.
Players have long loved the electricity of playing night matches under the lights in the nation's biggest city.
But the tournament had already set a record with three post-2am finishes over the first six days, as well as having two other matches go past 1am.
